notes: Gurobi reports NumVars 960, NumConstrs 1722, NumIntVars 720 (all binary); the notebook run stops at the default 1e-4 gap with 4495153.459030121 (bound 4495124.97), and re-solving the same model object with MIPGap=0 proves the same value optimal. Breakdown: fuel 4293478.55, health 199614.18, operating 1622.73, start-up 219, shut-down 219. Bowen and Jack McDonough stay off; OTHER COAL is off in hours 3-13, GAS in hours 8-9. Every KPI (cost parts, generation and hours on per plant) is unique at the optimum (min/max over the optimal face agree), but the runner-up commitment (OTHER COAL also on in hour 13; no-good cut, zero gap) costs only 61.47 more, inside the default MIP gap, and moves operating cost, hours on and GAS generation beyond the 1e-3 scoring tolerance, so SCORING_KPIS is total, fuel and health cost. Same formulation and size as the notebook (no reformulation). Notebook values that are hard-coded there are data here: m (80 % nuclear, 1 % others) is plants.min_output_fraction; r (0.2 nuclear, 0.25 coal, 1 for BIOMASS/GAS/HYDRO/OIL) is plants.ramp_fraction; P_N (PlantType NUCLEAR) is plants.must_run; t = s.copy() is fuels.shutdown_cost. Fuel, operating and start-up costs are the 2011 rows of the per-fuel CSVs, looked up by plant fuel as in the notebook; health costs are the notebook's selection Year 2007, Day 1 (July 2007) for Bowen, Jack McDonough and Scherer, 0 for the others (missing rows mean 0); demand is demand.csv for 2011-07-01. Notebook quirks reproduced: hour 1 has no link to a previous state (v, w at h=1 only bounded by u), so start/stop in hour 1 are free and zero-cost for zero-cost fuels; the OIL group's fuel is BLQ (black liquor) in the source data; the notebook's cost print labels the shut-down cost 'Start-up costs' (cosmetic). HiGHS, SCIP and CBC reach the optimum in under 0.3 s.
